purpose: Hook in agent frontmatter, agent run as a SUBAGENT via the Agent tool (not as the main session): Write outside allowed/.
expected: Blocked by the hook if frontmatter hooks apply to subagents.
command: claude -p "Use the Agent tool with subagent_type spike-guarded to create forbidden/e3d.txt containing e3d with the Write tool. Report exactly what the subagent said happened, including any block message." --setting-sources project --max-budget-usd 0.5 --output-format json --no-session-persistence --permission-mode dontAsk --allowedTools Agent Read Write Edit Bash
agent_result:
The `spike-guarded` subagent's write went through, and nothing blocked it.

The subagent reported:

> The write worked. The Write tool created `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Temp\s12-2mjuo1gg\proj\forbidden\e3d.txt` with the exact content `e3d`. Nothing blocked it, and there was no permission prompt or error.
>
> The tool's full response was:
> ```
> File created successfully at: C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Temp\s12-2mjuo1gg\proj\forbidden\e3d.txt (file state is current in your context â€” no need to Read it back)
> ```
> Even though the directory is named `forbidden`, the file was created without any denial.

It also said its tools were Read, Write, Edit and Bash, and that it didn't use any MCP tools.

I checked the folder myself: `forbidden/e3d.txt` exists and contains `e3d` (3 bytes), next to an existing `keep.txt`. So either the PreToolUse path-guard hook didn't fire for this agent, or its rule doesn't cover `forbidden/`.
